Case notes, Dispute #61190: Customer Elena Vance called to report that her ex-business-partner, Marcus Webb, made an unauthorized transfer of $4,200 from their former joint business account before it was closed. She states she never agreed to any final withdrawal and wants the funds returned.

Mr. Webb was contacted for comment on 10 Sep; he states the transfer was his final partner draw, pre-approved in their dissolution agreement signed by both parties on August 1st, and provided a scanned copy of that agreement showing what appears to be Ms. Vance's signature authorizing exactly this amount.

Follow-up call to Ms. Vance, 12 Sep: agent read her the relevant clause from Mr. Webb's copy of the agreement and asked her to confirm whether the signature was hers. Ms. Vance said she needed to check her own paperwork and would call back; she has not called back as of this note.

Supervisor note, 15 Sep: case remains open pending Ms. Vance's response on the signature question. Do not release or reverse any funds until she confirms one way or the other, or until 30 days have passed with no response, per standard dispute-aging policy.

Dispute-aging policy (referenced above): per section 9.4 of the account agreement, if a dispute over funds movement between joint or former-joint account holders cannot be resolved through voluntary confirmation from both parties within 30 calendar days of being opened, the case is escalated to the bank's internal arbitration team, who may request additional documentation before issuing a binding determination.

Additional follow-up, 20 Sep: Ms. Vance's attorney contacted the bank on her behalf, requesting a 15-day extension before she responds to the signature question, citing the need to have the document reviewed by a forensic document examiner. The bank granted the extension per its discretion under section 9.4; the new response deadline is now 5 Oct. Mr. Webb was notified of the extension and did not object, though he did ask that the funds remain frozen rather than released to either party in the meantime, which is already the default under the open-case hold.

Case owner's note, 20 Sep: given the extension, this case is now expected to remain open until at least early October. No party has withdrawn their claim, and no new evidence beyond Mr. Webb's copy of the agreement has been submitted by either side. Both parties have been reminded that the joint account itself was already closed prior to this dispute, so any funds ultimately deemed to belong to Ms. Vance would need to be paid out from the bank's holding account rather than reversed as a simple transaction.

state:
Customer service log, ticket #40021:

9:02am -- Customer reported the couch cushions delivered with order #40021 were 'the wrong color, nothing like the photos on the listing,' and attached two photos of the couch in their living room.

9:15am -- Agent compared the customer's photos to the product listing photos. Noted that the listing photos were taken in a studio with warm, even indoor lighting, while the customer's photos were taken near a large window with strong daylight streaming in, which can shift how fabric color reads significantly, sometimes making warm greys look cool blue-grey or vice versa.

9:20am -- Agent requested a close-up photo of the fabric tag, which lists the exact color code, to compare against the listing's stated color code directly rather than relying on visual comparison alone.

9:34am -- Customer sent the tag photo. Agent confirmed the color code, fabric composition, and stitching pattern on the tag all matched the listing exactly, with zero discrepancies.

9:40am -- Agent explained the lighting effect to the customer, who replied: 'oh, that would explain it, never mind, I just looked at it again in the lamp light and it actually looks exactly like the pictures now, sorry for the trouble.'

9:41am -- Ticket closed, no replacement or refund issued, none requested by customer at close.

Supervisor QA review, added same day: Reviewed this ticket as part of routine quality sampling. Agent followed the correct verification protocol for color-mismatch claims by requesting the fabric tag rather than relying on photo comparison alone, consistent with policy section 12.3 on visual-discrepancy disputes. No refund, replacement, or discount was issued, which is appropriate since the investigation found the product matched the listing exactly and the customer confirmed satisfaction after the lighting explanation. Ticket correctly closed with no further action needed. For reference, this is the third color-mismatch ticket this month resolved the same way once a tag-code comparison was done instead of a photo-only comparison; the other two also turned out to be lighting-related rather than genuine mismatches. No pattern of actual color-mismatch defects has been found across any of these three cases this month, so no changes to the product listing or its photos are recommended at this time either. Recommend adding a short line to the returns FAQ suggesting customers photograph items in natural daylight near a window before filing a color-mismatch claim, since that lighting condition has now come up in all three of this month's cases.
